note: Written by Claude from reputable outlets (Yahoo Finance/Reuters, ABS, Al Jazeera, The Standard, Bernama, PTI, Japan Times and others); source under each story. Some sections are shorter today because fewer verified reports were retrievable. Sports excluded.

items.headline: Microsoft beats on cloud; shares jump after hours
items.summary: Fiscal first-quarter earnings came in at $4.89 a share on $92.28bn of revenue, ahead of forecasts of $4.73 and $90.63bn. Cloud revenue reached $63.9bn. The stock rose about 4% in after-hours trade.

items.headline: Alphabet profit misses; stock slides about 9% late
items.summary: Earnings of $2.12 a share fell well short of the roughly $2.99 expected, and revenue was marginally below forecasts. Alphabet said its Gemini app now has 1 billion users, but shares fell around 8.7% after hours.

items.headline: Oracle soars 10.7% on long-range revenue goal
items.summary: The database and cloud company said it expects at least $225bn in revenue in fiscal 2030, implying annual growth above 35%.

items.headline: Samsung reportedly to quit Hong Kong home-appliance market
items.summary: The Korean group is said to be preparing to stop selling fridges, washing machines and air-conditioners in Hong Kong, after earlier pulling out of mainland China's appliance business.

items.headline: Moody's: AI build-out is swelling private credit
items.summary: The ratings agency said borrowing for AI infrastructure is expanding the private-credit market, and warned that a wall of maturing loans could leave weaker borrowers struggling to refinance.

items.headline: Fed holds rates at 3.75%–4% but two officials want a hike
items.summary: The vote was 10-2, with Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack and Governor Lisa Cook dissenting in favour of raising rates. Traders now price about an 85% chance of a quarter-point hike at the 9 December meeting.

items.headline: Wall Street edges higher after the Fed
items.summary: The S&P 500 closed up 0.28% at 7,743.98, the Dow rose 0.19% to 52,475.10 and the Nasdaq gained 0.27%, before Microsoft and Alphabet results moved futures after the bell.

items.headline: Oil rises after attack on Saudi refinery
items.summary: December US crude gained 1.77% to about $101.67 a barrel following reports of an attack on a Saudi Arabian refinery.

items.headline: Trian bids $1.4bn for Wendy's
items.summary: Shares of the burger chain jumped about 15% after reports that Nelson Peltz's Trian Partners offered to buy the company. Robinhood fell nearly 8% in early trade after a third-quarter earnings miss.

items.headline: Chinese PCB maker dips on Hong Kong debut
items.summary: Suzhou Dongshan Precision closed slightly lower on its first day of trading after raising HK$9.88bn in its share sale.

items.headline: Ministers tell haze-linked firms 'business as usual' is over
items.summary: Senior Minister K Shanmugam, DPM Gan Kim Yong and Minister Grace Fu met leaders of 10 Singapore-registered palm oil and forestry firms served NEA notices, including Wilmar, Golden Agri and Asia Pulp & Paper. All agreed to cooperate; they must hire independent assessors at their own cost, and tougher haze laws are being studied for the next Parliament sitting.

items.headline: EMA hires nuclear consultants ahead of 2027 IAEA review
items.summary: The Energy Market Authority has appointed nuclear consultants and law firms to prepare for a review by the UN nuclear watchdog that will judge whether Singapore is ready to make an informed decision on nuclear power.

items.headline: Afternoon showers bring some relief from haze
items.summary: Air quality eased on Wednesday as rain fell across the island, raising hopes of clearer skies.

items.headline: Hegseth pitches new US-ASEAN defence framework in Cebu
items.summary: At the ASEAN defence ministers' meetings in the Philippines, the US Defense Secretary proposed what he called an ambitious new defence framework with the bloc.

items.headline: Malaysia offers Indonesia help fighting forest fires
items.summary: Kuala Lumpur offered operational support and technology cooperation; Indonesia's disaster agency BNPB is reviewing the offer as the regional haze persists.

items.headline: Thailand offers up to 50,000 baht per home for rooftop solar
items.summary: The programme targets one million households, aiming to lower power bills and expand clean energy.

items.headline: Thai police smash mule-account network
items.summary: Eleven suspects were arrested in a nationwide operation against a transnational ring selling corporate mule accounts to scam gangs and money launderers.

items.headline: About 200 cruise passengers stranded in Cambodia
items.summary: Passengers on a 'Cruise for life' voyage were left stuck at a Cambodian port after the operator ran out of money.

items.headline: Takaichi and Merz pledge closer economic-security ties
items.summary: Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi and German Chancellor Friedrich Merz agreed to strengthen cooperation on economic security and technology during his visit.

items.headline: Defence build-up runs into funding roadblocks
items.summary: Tokyo's push to expand defence spending faces financing hurdles, including the contentious question of tax increases.

items.headline: Bank of Japan seen holding rates this week
items.summary: The central bank is unlikely to raise its policy rate at its meeting this week, according to a Japan Times preview.

items.headline: SK hynix profit jumps sevenfold; memory sold out to 2029
items.summary: September-quarter operating profit hit 83.3 trillion won (about $62.5bn), beating forecasts. The chipmaker plans to return 60 trillion won to shareholders and says its memory capacity is sold out through 2029.

items.headline: Kospi surges about 6.6% on chip rally
items.summary: Seoul's benchmark posted a huge one-day gain on Wednesday as SK hynix rose about 11% and Samsung Electronics about 9%.

items.headline: Samsung Electronics results due today
items.summary: Investors are watching Samsung's quarterly report on Thursday for further signs of AI-driven memory demand and pricing, after the Kospi fell 1.46% on Monday in the run-up.

items.headline: Inflation jumps to 4.3%, raising odds of a rate hike
items.summary: Annual CPI rose to 4.3% in September from 4.0%, with prices up 1.3% over the quarter. Underlying (trimmed-mean) inflation was 3.6%; fuel rose 9.4% in the month on higher oil prices, and housing was the biggest contributor. The RBA meets next week.

items.headline: Democrats lead by 9 points with six days to the midterms
items.summary: A Reuters/Ipsos poll put Democrats ahead 50% to 41% including leaners; Trump's approval was 32%, and 73% said the cost of living is on the wrong track. Election day is 3 November.

items.headline: Trump rallies in Ohio; Obama campaigns in Georgia
items.summary: Trump held his third Ohio rally of the month, while Obama joined Senator Jon Ossoff and governor candidate Keisha Lance Bottoms in Atlanta.

items.headline: Tight Senate races in Texas, Ohio and Kansas worry Republicans
items.summary: Texas's Talarico–Paxton contest is virtually tied, and over $400m has been spent or reserved in Ohio's Brown–Husted race. Small third-party votes could decide several seats.

items.headline: Crypto industry pours $176m into midterms
items.summary: The sector is spending heavily on the elections as it prepares for politics after Trump.

items.headline: Former vice premier Liu Yandong dies
items.summary: The former Politburo member, a long-serving senior woman in the leadership, died in Beijing on Wednesday, Xinhua reported.

items.headline: Hong Kong fire inquiry report handed to Chief Executive
items.summary: The independent committee on the Wang Fuk Court fire has submitted its report; the government may publish it and proposed reforms, including criminalising bid-rigging, as soon as Thursday.

items.headline: Hong Kong rents hit another record
items.summary: Rents set a fresh high last month and home prices rose for a second month, driven by demand from expatriates and mainland talent.

items.headline: Cyclone Arnab hits Andhra Pradesh; 180,000 evacuated
items.summary: The 'very severe' storm made landfall early Wednesday with winds up to 135 km/h, affecting areas including Kakinada and Visakhapatnam, before weakening inland.

items.headline: Rupee slips to 95.28 as Brent tops $115
items.summary: A firmer dollar and higher crude pushed the rupee down 21 paise. The Sensex fell 352 points to 73,246 and the Nifty closed at 22,699.
